metadata.name: Vite Client-Side Webapp
metadata.description: A framework-free, server-free Vite single-page app with a pure domain core, feature slices behind public entries, and all browser platform APIs isolated in adapters. Derived from the user-supplied blueprint and verified against the observed import graph of dcassil/simpleCam.

evidence.detail: Single bootstrap file: imports styles, constructs the platform camera adapter, resolves #app, calls createApp.

evidence.section: Import direction is STRICT and downward only
evidence.detail: entry(src/main.ts) -> app, styles, platform, shared
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

entry.tradeoffs: A one-file module keeps bootstrap logic out of app. Any second bootstrap file would need the mapping widened.

evidence.detail: Composition root wiring the app shell and the capture feature with injected platform adapter.

evidence.section: Import direction is STRICT and downward only
evidence.detail: app -> features (ONLY via index.ts), ui, platform, shared
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

app.tradeoffs: One file today; the directory mapping anticipates growth. Low cost.

evidence.detail: Public entry of the capture feature; re-exports mountCaptureView.

evidence.section: Import direction is STRICT and downward only
evidence.detail: features are imported only via src/features/<name>/index.ts
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

features.tradeoffs: Each feature must maintain an index.ts. Small ongoing discipline cost; it is already followed.

evidence.detail: Feature-local implementation, imported only by the capture index.
Pattern matched by negating index.ts under src/features/*; the matcher cannot distinguish same-feature from cross-feature internals.

feature-internals.tradeoffs: The two negated glob patterns are copied from the blueprint and have not been verified against the Shore Guard matcher. If they do not resolve, feature-internals becomes an empty module and the deep-import rules silently stop matching. Verify with shore-guard check after adoption.

evidence.detail: Presentational DOM shell; imports nothing internal.
Presentational status paragraph; imports nothing internal.

evidence.section: Import direction is STRICT and downward only
evidence.detail: ui -> domain, shared
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

ui.tradeoffs: UI files touch the DOM but not device APIs. The boundary is only an import boundary; DOM usage inside ui is intended.

evidence.detail: Pure types and functions for camera status; no imports, no DOM globals.

evidence.section: Import direction is STRICT and downward only
evidence.detail: domain -> shared; domain must not reference window, document, or navigator
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

domain.tradeoffs: Import rules cannot detect use of window/document/navigator globals (blueprint open question 2); that part of the intent stays unenforced until a no-dom-globals rule kind exists.

evidence.detail: Only file that references navigator.mediaDevices; exposes a CameraAdapter interface typed with domain types.
camera-adapter.ts imports type CameraStatus

evidence.detail: platform -> domain, shared; only platform may call browser device APIs
User-supplied Vite client-side blueprint states the same layer graph; no catalog preset matches a framework-free, server-free Vite SPA.

platform.tradeoffs: All device API access funnels through adapters, which adds an interface per capability but keeps features testable.

shared.tradeoffs: Shared must stay a leaf; anything needing another layer has to move out of shared.

evidence.detail: The compile target is a browser bundle; no Node type library is included.
Only Vite client ambient types are available to src/.
No runtime dependencies exist; vite is tooling only.
The only import of the vite package lives in the root config, outside src/.
Blueprint forbids Node builtins and build tooling from all runtime modules because this is a browser-only bundle.

node-builtins.tradeoffs: Package-name mapping, not a directory; it exists only so runtime modules can forbid it. The builtin list is the blueprint list and may need additions.

build-tooling.tradeoffs: Package-name mapping for vite and vitest. vitest is not installed today; listing it is pre-emptive.
